Interactive Production-Engine Backtest

Backtest the Deleverage Shield on your own data

Upload historical price CSVs for up to five tokens and run Proteus (v18), the volatility-scaled adaptive Deleverage Shield, against plain Buy & Hold. Both receive identical DCA capital on the same schedule, so the only difference is the exposure control itself: how far the shield pulls risk off the table in stress, and what that costs in upside.

Your CSV is parsed in your browser. Only the resulting price series is sent to the engine, where it is processed in memory and discarded — never stored, never logged. The run happens on the server because the modulator's parameters stay there and are never shipped to the browser. Results are scored on risk-adjusted return (Sharpe and Calmar), not on whether they beat Buy & Hold in raw percent.

Proteus (v18) is live This tab runs one engine: Proteus (v18), the production shield — the same volatility-scaled adaptive code path a live portfolio is replayed through every day, with thresholds that auto-tune to both calm large-cap baskets and high-vol alt baskets. The former Aegis (v14) comparison leg is retired from the backtest; v14 still runs in production only as a warm-up fallback for portfolios too young to calibrate the adaptive threshold.

Hypothetical results. This page computes a simulation from the price history you upload. A backtest applies a strategy to the past with complete knowledge of how that period turned out — knowledge nobody had at the time — and it ignores slippage, spreads and taxes, though it does charge a simulated 0.1% exchange fee on every rebalance, DCA buy and redeployment. Hypothetical and past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. AQMath is software for your own analysis: it is not investment advice, not a recommendation to buy or sell any asset, and it never places orders or holds funds.

How it works

Upload historical price CSVs for your tokens (up to 5). Every run executes the production engine — Proteus (v18), volatility-scaled dynamic thresholds with V-bounce re-entry — on your basket, capital and DCA schedule, next to Buy & Hold, which buys tokens unconditionally and stays fully exposed. The basket follows the same 180-day macro loop as production — a KKT risk-parity re-optimisation every 180 days on the trailing 180-day window. Both legs charge the same simulated fees and redeploy parked DCA cash the same way, and results are scored on risk-adjusted return (Sharpe and Calmar), not on beating Buy & Hold.
